number.description: Slot number: the identifier every action accepts, alongside the email and the alias

headroomPct.description: Quota left in the binding window (0-100); null when the usage is unknown

scoped.description: Per-model weekly windows (Fable, Opus…) when the account reports them

pct.description: Share of the window already consumed (0-100)

countdown.description: Human countdown to the reset, e.g. `3h 4m`

name.description: Per-model windows carry the model name

AccountUsageWindow.description: One rate-limit window as claude-swap reports it.

account.description: claude-swap account this run is pinned to, when it is not using the active one

workflows.description: Claude Code workflows it ran (the Workflow tool), with each agent's progress

workingDir.description: Directory the CLI actually works in, which differs from `cwd` when it runs in a worktree

permissionPrompts.description: Where its prompts go; kept so a resumed run asks the same way

pendingPrompts.description: Prompts waiting for someone right now: the run is stuck until they are answered

runId.description: Empty when the task belongs to a CLI session rather than a run

source.description: `run` when read from a run's live stream, `disk` when read from its session's files

command.description: The shell command, when it is a backgrounded Bash call

backgroundedByUser.description: Sent to the background by the person at the terminal rather than by the model

fromSubagent.description: Launched by a subagent rather than by the main agent (`owned_by_subagent` on the stream event)

ownerAgentId.description: The subagent that launched it, when known. The stream event only says a subagent did, so this comes from the subagent's own transcript, where the launch result is recorded.

BackgroundTask.description: Work the CLI runs in the background: a Bash command sent there (by the model or by the person at the terminal), a monitor, a remote agent. The CLI calls every delegated piece of work a task, and reports foreground commands that way too; those are left out, and so are subagents and workflows, which have lists of their own.

worktree.description: Set when `path` is inside a git worktree of that project

WorkLocation.description: Where a piece of work happens, resolved to the project it belongs to. A worktree resolves to its repository, so work spread across worktrees still reads as one project.

runId.description: Empty when the subagent belongs to a CLI session rather than a run

status.description: `stopped` when its session ended before the agent reported back

source.description: `run` when read from a run's live stream, `cli` when read from a session's files on disk

sessionId.description: Session that spawned it; always set for `cli` subagents

agentId.description: The CLI's own id for the agent

lastActivityAt.description: Last time the agent wrote to its transcript

cwd.description: Directory the agent works in, from its own transcript: a worktree when started with isolation

background.description: Launched to run in the background, rather than awaited by its parent

SubagentInfo.description: An agent a session spawned with the Agent tool, in the foreground or the background.

id.description: The CLI's workflow run id (`wf_…`) when known, the task id otherwise

status.description: `stopped` when its session ended before the workflow reported back

runId.description: Empty when the workflow belongs to a CLI session rather than a run

source.description: `run` when read from a run's live stream, `cli` when read from a session's files on disk

result.description: What the script returned, once it finished

WorkflowRun.description: A run of a Claude Code workflow: a script started with the Workflow tool that orchestrates subagents inside one session. Read from a run's live stream (`local_workflow` tasks) or from the files the CLI keeps beside the session's transcript.

state.description: As the CLI reports it: `start`, `progress`, `done` or `error`

WorkflowAgentState.description: One agent a workflow launched, as its progress reports it.

worktree.description: From the CLI's own record, when the session ran in a worktree it created

taskId.description: Task id inside the orchestration; `__synthesis__` for the final report

SessionOriginKind.description: Who created a session, so the UI can group the wrapper's own sessions under their parent:   cli           started outside the wrapper (terminal, IDE…)   run           a run started from the wrapper (UI or API)   orchestration a worker (or the synthesis step) of an orchestration   internal      housekeeping runs of the wrapper itself (planner, auth check); hidden by default

detail.description: Model reply, or the CLI error

state.description: What the CLI reports for a background agent: `done`, `blocked`…

live.description: Whether this is a session actually open for work. A process the CLI reports as `done`, and a pre-warmed spare that never received a user turn, are both listed but not live: they still hold a pid worth seeing, yet counting them was what made the panel claim sessions nobody had.

runId.description: Set when it maps to a run managed by the wrapper

ActiveCliSession.description: CLI sessions alive on the machine/container (`claude agents --json`)

temporary.description: Lives under the OS temp dir (scratch/test directories)

id.description: Encoded directory name inside ~/.claude/projects

activeRuns.description: Wrapper runs currently alive inside this project

activeSessions.description: CLI sessions live in this directory that no run owns — work started from a terminal

parentId.description: Set when this directory is a git worktree: the repository it belongs to

createdBy.description: The orchestration task that created this worktree, when one did

gitUrl.description: Clone this repository instead of creating an empty directory

entries.description: The window of the transcript this page carries, oldest first

from.description: Index of the first entry in `entries` within the whole transcript

total.description: Entries the transcript holds in total, so a caller knows what is still above `from`

hits.description: Hits in transcript order, oldest first: one per entry, however many times it matches

total.description: Entries (or events) searched, the same `total` a page of the transcript reports

truncated.description: More entries matched than `hits` carries; the oldest ones were left out

index.description: Index of the entry or event, in the same index space as `from` and `total` of a page

snippet.description: The text around the first match, whitespace collapsed

kind.description: For a run, the kind of event the hit is in, so a view that hides some kinds can skip them

TranscriptSearchHit.description: One entry (or run event) whose text contains the query.

RunEventKind.description: `partial` events are ephemeral: they carry the text generated so far for the block being streamed, reuse the seq of the last stored event, are never buffered or replayed, and are superseded by the next `message` event.

attachments.description: Uploads (`POST /uploads`) attached to the first message

cwd.description: Working directory; defaults to the wrapper workspace

forkSession.description: With `resumeSessionId`: continue in a copy (`--fork-session`), a new session with the same history, leaving the original untouched. The way to pick up a session that is still open in a terminal without two processes writing the same conversation.

worktree.description: Run inside a new git worktree of this name, created and managed by the CLI (`--worktree`)

maxBudgetUsd.description: Hard ceiling on what this run may spend, enforced by the CLI (`--max-budget-usd`)

permissionPrompts.description: Who answers what the CLI would ask a person: tool permissions, `AskUserQuestion`, plan approval. `host` sends them to the panel (`GET /runs/:id/permissions`); `none`, the default, denies them, which is the only safe choice for a client that is not going to answer.

keepAlive.description: Keep the process alive after each turn so more messages can be sent (default true)

internal.description: Housekeeping run: no transcript is written (`--no-session-persistence`), so it cannot be resumed

account.description: Pin the run to a claude-swap account (slot number, email or alias) instead of the active one. Runs through `cswap run`, which needs claude-swap installed.

events.description: The window of the run's events this page carries, oldest first

from.description: Index of the first event in `events` within everything the run has emitted

total.description: Events the run has emitted in total

type.description: Original type/subtype of the stream-json event

block.description: For `partial` events: which kind of block is streaming

EffectiveEnvironment.description: What Claude Code actually loaded for a directory, taken from the `init` event of the most recent wrapper run there (the CLI only reports it when a session starts).

output.description: Without `offset`, the tail of the file (at most 64 KiB); with it, up to 64 KiB of what follows that byte, so a longer gap takes several reads (`offset` < `bytes` means more is waiting)

truncated.description: `output` is the tail of a longer file, not its start. Never set on a read that resumed from `offset`.

bytes.description: Size of the output file in bytes

offset.description: Byte position just after `output`: pass it back as `?offset=` to read only what came since

reset.description: The requested `offset` was past the end of the file (it was replaced), so `output` restarts from the tail

BackgroundTaskOutput.description: Captured output of a background task, as the CLI wrote it.

workflowRunId.description: The workflow run (`wf_…`) a workflow agent belongs to

toolUseId.description: The Agent tool call that spawned it; workflow agents have none

description.description: The description given at launch; a workflow agent's is its label

prompt.description: Its first message: the prompt it was given

status.description: `stopped` when its session ended before the agent reported back

result.description: Text of the agent's last assistant message: what it reported back

entries.description: Entries of the transcript, from index `from` on (all of it unless `?after=` asked for a tail)

from.description: Index of the first entry returned

total.description: Entries in the whole transcript: pass it back as `?after=` to read only what was appended

tasks.description: Background tasks this agent launched, where the transcripts say so (subagents only)

AgentTranscript.description: Everything one subagent or workflow agent did, from the transcript and meta the CLI keeps for it beside the session's transcript: what it was asked, how it went, and its whole conversation.

AgentTokenUsage.description: Token usage summed over an agent's assistant messages.

WorkflowDefinition.description: A saved workflow the Workflow tool can run by name, from a `.claude/workflows/` directory.

cwd.description: Project to run it in; its `.claude/workflows/` must hold it unless it is a user workflow

args.description: Handed to the script as its `args`

RunWorkflowRequest.description: Starts a run that runs a saved workflow.

name.description: File and workflow name; defaults to one derived from the graph's

overwrite.description: Replace a saved workflow of the same name

SaveOrchestrationWorkflowRequest.description: Copies the script a workflow graph ran into the project's `.claude/workflows/`.

worktree.description: Each task gets its own git worktree and branch instead of sharing the checkout

permissionPrompts.description: Where a worker's permission prompts go

baseCommit.description: Commit every worktree branches from, recorded when the graph starts

integration.description: The one branch a worktree graph delivers, built once its tasks finish

synthesisRunId.description: The synthesis run, so its report can be continued like any other conversation

workflow.description: The workflow engine's run and script, when the graph runs as a workflow

worktree.description: Git worktree this task works in, when the orchestration isolates its workers

commit.description: Commit the wrapper made of work the worker left uncommitted, when there was any

worktree.description: Worktree the branch is checked out in, until the worktrees are removed

merged.description: Tasks whose branch is contained in the integration branch

conflicts.description: Merges that conflicted, with the paths that did

commit.description: Head of the integration branch once merged

IntegrationStatus.description:
- `merging`: task branches are being merged into the integration branch
- `resolving`: a merge conflicted and an integrator agent is resolving it
- `merged`: every completed task's work is on the branch
- `conflicted`: the integrator could not finish; the branch is left for a person
- `failed`: integration could not run at all

OrchestrationEngine.description: How a graph runs:   graph     every task is its own `claude -p` process, optionally in its own worktree and branch,             merged into one integration branch at the end   workflow  every task is a subagent of one Claude Code session, driven by a workflow script             Agentry generates from the graph: cheaper and resumable from cache, but in the             project directory, so for work that does not change files in parallel

scriptPath.description: Script generated from the graph, in the wrapper's data directory

runId.description: The run whose session runs the workflow; a resume continues it

workflowRunId.description: The CLI's workflow run id (`wf_…`), which a resume replays from cache

engineReason.description: Why the planner chose the engine, shown next to it in the draft

synthesize.description: Launch a final agent that synthesizes the results

worktree.description: Give every task its own git worktree and branch, so parallel workers never write over each other — and never edit the checkout the wrapper itself is running from.

allowedTools.description: Tools every worker may use without being asked. A worker has no one to ask unless `permissionPrompts` sends its prompts to the panel, so anything it needs beyond editing files has to be pre-authorised here or approved there.

permissionPrompts.description: `host` routes each worker's permission prompts to the panel for a person to answer

PlanDraftSummary.description: A planner run's draft, kept so a plan is never lost with the response that carried it.

toolUseId.description: The CLI's id for the tool call this decides

input.description: Arguments the tool would be called with, e.g. the shell command

description.description: The CLI's own one-line description of the call

suggestions.description: Rules the CLI offers to remember, e.g. switching to acceptEdits; send them back to accept

requiresUserInteraction.description: Waits on a person by design (a question), rather than on an approval

PermissionRequest.description: A tool call the CLI is holding until someone decides. Questions (`AskUserQuestion`) and plan approval (`ExitPlanMode`) arrive this way too: they are answered by allowing them, with the answers in `updatedInput`.

PermissionUpdate.description: A permission rule or mode change, exactly as the CLI proposes it.

message.description: Shown to the model when denying, so it can adapt instead of guessing

updatedInput.description: Lets the approver edit the arguments before allowing them, or carries a question's answers

updatedPermissions.description: Suggestions from the request to apply when allowing ("always allow")

RunSettingsUpdate.description: What can be changed on a run without restarting it. A live process takes it at once.

ResumeOrchestrationRequest.description: Settings that can be corrected when resuming, so a graph started with the wrong ones is fixed and picked up instead of rebuilt. Only what shapes the workers still to run; completed work is kept.
